title: Inheritance Scam Alerts: Remote-Control Requests, Pay-First 'Unlocks', and Telling Real from Fake
plain:
If a 'support technician' says the only fix for your wallet software is installing AnyDesk or similar remote-control software, it is a scam. Remote-control software requests are always a scam - no legitimate support needs control of your computer. Stop contact immediately: install nothing, hang up or close the chat, and delete the message.

A sympathetic stranger - even one who shares your story, like a widow whose kids also inherited crypto - may ask you to send 0.001 bitcoin first to 'unlock' the estate transfer her family received. Send-a-small-amount-first is always a scam: nothing is ever unlocked by paying first. Stop contact and do nothing; your bitcoin stays safe exactly where it is.

You do not need to become paranoid about everything - just learn five signals. It is a scam if they ask for words or keys, urge speed, ask for a test payment, want remote access, or contacted you first. No legitimate company asks for your words - not wallet makers, exchanges, banks, or anyone claiming to represent the estate.

Your safe default costs nothing: you lose nothing by ignoring every such message. If something matters, it will still be true tomorrow. Verify it yourself through official channels - this app, or contact details you find on your own, never a link or number from the message.
technical:
Remote-access pattern: fraudsters posing as wallet or exchange 'support' direct targets to install remote-control software, then observe recovery words, swap receiving addresses, or install malware. Any unsolicited request for remote control of a machine that touches wallet software or key material is fraud; stop contact immediately and install nothing. Advance-fee pattern: a small 'unlocking' or 'activation' payment (e.g., 0.001 BTC) required before an inheritance is released is advance-fee fraud; no Bitcoin mechanism requires prepayment to release funds.

Classification heuristic: an inbound message is a scam if it requests seed words or keys, manufactures urgency, requests a test payment, requests remote access, or initiated contact first. Ignore-and-delete has zero cost, so it is the safe default.

claims.claim: Remote-control software requests are always a scam.
No legitimate support needs control of your computer.
If a 'support technician' asks you to install remote-control software such as AnyDesk, stop contact immediately.
Nothing is ever unlocked by paying first.
If someone says a small payment such as 0.001 bitcoin will unlock an estate transfer, stop contact and do nothing.
It is a scam if they ask for words or keys, urge speed, ask for a test payment, want remote access, or contacted you first.
No legitimate company asks for your words.
You lose nothing by ignoring every such message.

warnings: Never install remote-control software (e.g., AnyDesk) at the request of anyone who contacted you; it grants full access to your computer and anything you type.
Never send any amount of bitcoin - even 0.001 - to 'unlock', 'activate', or 'release' a transfer or inheritance; sent coins cannot be recovered.
Never type, speak, or photograph your recovery words for anyone; anyone who asks is a scammer.
Do not reset, wipe, or 'clean' any device until your backup is verified - a scammer's scare story is never a reason to reset.
